prompt: Which snippet correctly implements equals() for a class with a single int field 'id'?
choices: @Override public boolean equals(Object o) { return this.id == o.id; }
@Override public boolean equals(Object o) { if (!(o instanceof MyClass c)) return false; return this.id == c.id; }
@Override public boolean equals(MyClass o) { return this.id == o.id; }
public static boolean equals(MyClass a, MyClass b) { return a.id == b.id; }
explanation: equals() takes Object, not the concrete type. You must check instanceof before casting. Option A: o.id won't compile — o is Object. Option C: overloads but doesn't override equals(Object). Option D: static equals doesn't override Object.equals().
